status: initial tolerances fixed before first numerical comparison; keys/values criterion revised after the first comparison (see tolerance_changes)
notes: FP32 official eager attention versus FP32 ONNX CPU. Any tolerance change needs an explanation in the proof report. All elements must be finite; shapes must match exactly. Transcript equality does not waive numerical failures.
scoring: NFKC; ASCII lowercase; ignore punctuation; join apostrophes inside words. Mandarin CER counts Chinese characters and ASCII letters/digits. English WER counts words. Mixed MER counts Chinese characters and English words. No simplified/traditional conversion. Displayed text is unchanged.
criteria: A stage passes when every element satisfies |native-reference| <= absolute + relative*|reference|. Stages that also define scale_relative/rmse_relative pass alternatively when max|native-reference| <= absolute + scale_relative*max|reference| and RMSE <= rmse_relative*RMS(reference) over the whole tensor. Shapes must match exactly and all elements must be finite.

tolerance_changes.reason: Decoder KV caches contain attention-sink outliers with magnitudes up to about 390 (keys) and 143 (values). FP32 accumulation-order differences between ONNX Runtime fused kernels and PyTorch eager appear as absolute noise of up to 0.06 spread over the tensor, not proportional to the individual element, so the element-wise rule fails on elements near zero although the tensor agrees to about 1e-4 of its scale. The decision quantity (logits) still meets the original element-wise tolerance (max error about 2e-4 against 0.005) and all 24 token sequences are identical to the oracle. Encoder, input_embeds, logits, mel and pcm tolerances are unchanged.
